The only credible public basis is aggregate readiness plus general governance principles around documenting and managing risk. That basis is materially weakened by the named-segment evaluation gap, the policy text tying named launch use cases to materiality, and the unresolved legal ticket. Product's non-core framing is not enough to neutralize materiality on the admissible record. The packet therefore should defend certification narrowly and explicitly acknowledge that the support for no-disclosure treatment is weak.

Operational readiness evidence is relevant but not sufficient when the governing policy makes materiality turn on named customer commitments and pending legal review.
